skill.name: kleros-curate
skill.description: Guide Kleros Curate registry work, including discovery, policy validation, item preparation, IPFS metadata, and reviewed onchain registry actions.
skill.summary: Prepare and verify Kleros Curate registry operations before users submit onchain transactions.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: All 109 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, public registry endpoints, URL text, or blockchain metadata terminology. No prompt injection, malware behavior, credential collection, or unauthorized reconnaissance was found. The skill can prepare high-impact onchain actions, so every wallet action requires an explicit final review.

remediation.issue: Onchain actions can lock funds, spend tokens, or change governance when parameters are wrong.
remediation.suggestion: Before any wallet approval, display chain ID, target contract, method, calldata summary, native value, ERC20 approval amount, recipient, and irreversible effects. Require explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Public and private endpoint guidance can lead users to disclose API tokens or submit data to unverified services.
remediation.suggestion: Keep tokens out of prompts and logs. Require users to verify endpoint ownership and use public endpoints when private access is unnecessary.

semantic_findings.title: Irreversible Onchain Financial and Governance Actions
semantic_findings.description: The workflow prepares ERC20 approvals, permanent collateral, native-token payments, and administrative transactions. A mistaken target or parameter can lock funds or transfer registry control.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The document explicitly states that ERC20 collateral remains locked and that separate native-token payments are required. These outcomes are materially irreversible after a transaction confirms.

content.value_statement: Kleros registry actions require correct policy data, deposits, and contract details. This skill guides validation and transaction preparation for Curate workflows.
actual_capabilities: Identify Light Curate, Stake Curate, and Scout registry workflows.
Validate registry addresses, chain context, contract interfaces, and MetaEvidence schemas.
Prepare item metadata and explain IPFS publication requirements.
Calculate required deposits and distinguish native-token fees from ERC20 stakes.
Guide submission, challenge, evidence, appeal, withdrawal, and registry deployment workflows.
Provide checks before users approve or submit onchain transactions.
limitations: Cannot guarantee a contract, policy, endpoint, or token is legitimate.
Cannot reverse confirmed blockchain transactions or recover permanent stakes.
Requires users to provide correct chain, contract, wallet, and registry details.
Does not replace legal, financial, or smart contract security advice.

use_cases.title: Submit a curated token entry
use_cases.description: Prepare compliant metadata, deposits, and transaction details for an existing registry.

use_cases.title: Review a registry challenge
use_cases.description: Check policy rules, evidence requirements, and funding steps before contesting an item.

use_cases.title: Launch a new curated list
use_cases.description: Plan MetaEvidence, deployment parameters, and visibility verification for a new registry.

prompt_templates.title: Find registry type
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify whether this Kleros registry uses Light Curate or Stake Curate. I have chain ID and contract address.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare item submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a compliant item submission. Check required metadata, deposits, and confirmation steps before any transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Review challenge workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed challenge against registry policy. List evidence, deposits, deadlines, and risks. Do not submit a transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan safe deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a deployment review for a new PermanentGTCR registry. Verify each parameter, permissions, stake token, and irreversible consequence.

output_examples.input: Check my existing registry before submitting an item.
output: Required checks: chain, contract code, MetaEvidence schema, deposit
Action: review transaction target and value before signing

output_examples.input: What should I review before creating a Stake Curate list?
output: Review permanent ERC20 stake and native arbitration cost separately
Simulate deployment and record all parameters before approval
Prepare evidence and calculate challenge deposit
Confirm deadline, target contract, and transaction value before submission

best_practices: Read current onchain state and MetaEvidence before preparing any write transaction.
Show chain, contract address, method, token approval, recipient, and value before requesting confirmation.
Use a test environment or simulation before actions that lock funds or change governance.
anti_patterns: Do not sign transactions from unverified links, endpoints, or copied contract addresses.
Do not grant unlimited ERC20 approval when an exact approval is sufficient.
Do not submit placeholder metadata or assume a removed permanent stake is refundable.

faq.question: What registry types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Kleros Light Curate, Stake Curate, Scout, and related curated registry workflows.

faq.question: Can this skill submit transactions automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide transaction preparation, but users must review and approve each wallet action.

faq.question: Why must I inspect MetaEvidence?
faq.answer: MetaEvidence defines current registry policy and the required item metadata schema.

faq.question: Are Stake Curate deposits refundable?
faq.answer: Permanent ERC20 stakes can remain locked after item removal. Review registry rules before submitting.

faq.question: Does this skill verify project legitimacy?
faq.answer: No. It can check technical consistency, but users must independently verify projects and contracts.

faq.question: Can I use it for every token registry?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for Kleros Curate registries and not generic registry systems.
